text.p: Shares in Saint-Gobain were higher on the Paris Bourse on Wednesday after the company seemed more optimistic about its outlook than expected in a conference call with analysts following its first quarter results on Tuesday.
At 12256 GMT, Saint-Gobain was trading 1.53 percent higher at 794 francs while the CAC-40 blue chip index was 0.18 percent up at 2,656.74
"The statements by the company were more positive than I had expected, especially on the price trend in flat glass," said Andrew Melrose at Paribas Capital Markets.
Analysts who participated in the conference call were especially pleased to hear that the group had increased its flat glass price at the start of April and intended to increase them further in 1997.
Saint-Gobian raises the price of its 4mmm float by 10 percent on April 1 and aims to hike it by 20 percent in total in 1997.

"The new element which is making the share move was the increase in (flat glass) prices," said Emilio Alvarez at Morgan Stanley. He maintained his profit forecast, including exceptional items, at 5.85 billion francs for 1997.
Saint-Gobain made a 1996 net attributable income of 4.32 billion francs.
Melrose maintained his forecast at 5.68 billion francs including exceptionals, mainly a 1.36 billion franc gain from the sale of Cise.
